# Modern Web Guidance (Source) This repo is the source repository for [GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance) and includes the code and documentation for authoring, calibrating, and evaluating its contents. [**Modern Web Guidance**](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance) is a set of skills that embed web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data directly into your coding agents. It helps to steer your coding agents away from legacy patterns, and instead toward solutions that harness the power and capabilities of the modern web platform. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) and [GOVERNANCE.md](./GOVERNANCE.md) for how we work on the project and orientation of the codebase. --- *Stewarded by the Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and MDN teams, alongside the web development community.* [Documentation](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance) · [Eval Dashboard](https://googlechrome.github.io/modern-web-guidance-src/) · [Source Code](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src) · [Report an Issue](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src/issues) ## Quickstart ```shell npx modern-web-guidance@latest install ``` This command runs an interactive wizard to install Modern Web Guidance. See [Alternative Installation Methods](#-alternative-installation-methods) below. #### Try it out (without installing) ```shell # Search for relevant guides npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "animate a dialog modal backdrop" # Retrieve a guide by ID npx modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "animate-to-from-top-layer" # Scan a codebase for legacy patterns to modernize npx modern-web-guidance@latest legacy-scan . ``` ## Why? Coding agents often default to older patterns because LLM training data contains vast amounts of legacy code. This often leads them to generate bloated JavaScript for tasks that now have native, high-performance web platform solutions. Even if a model knows an API exists, it often lacks the density of real-world, modern implementation patterns required for production-ready code. **Modern Web Guidance bridges this gap.** Our skill's CLI returns targeted, expert-curated guidelines directly into your agent's context window, focusing on: * **Modern Browser APIs**: Helping models correctly structure APIs they frequently misuse. * **Performance & Accessibility**: Preferring platform-level APIs that can be optimized by the browser and include built-in accessibility affordances. * **Responsible Fallbacks**: Guiding models to use sensible, lightweight fallbacks instead of heavy polyfills or legacy libraries. ## What's Included? We cover the past several years of the web platform's new features, all the way up to the cutting edge. The guides are **designed to be token-efficient**; we run evals enabling us to prune lowest-common-denominator content that models already know. ### Core Disciplines

🎨 User Experience

Smooth visual states (View Transitions, entry/exit animations, parallax scroll, CSS scrollbar-color).

repositories.readme_excerpt: # Codex Security Codex Security helps you find, investigate, and fix vulnerabilities in your code. Use its security workflows in Codex, or automate them with the `@openai/codex-security` CLI and TypeScript SDK. - **In Codex:** [choose a security workflow](docs/agent-workflows.md). - **In a terminal:** [install the CLI and scan your repository](#quick-start). - **In automation:** use the [TypeScript SDK](#typescript-sdk) or [GitHub Action](#github-actions). ## Features - Scan repositories, selected paths, or Git changes. Deep scans repeat Standard scans and return their deduplicated findings. - Validate candidate findings, generate patches, and verify existing fixes. - Draft `SECURITY.md` policies and save threat models for later review. - Browse saved scans and findings, identify duplicates, assess severity against your own rubric, and suggest owners from source and Git history. - Preview third-party scanner findings, save them locally, or publish supported reports to Codex Security Cloud. [Scanner import guides](docs/scanner-imports/README.md). - Track findings in Linear, Jira, or GitHub, publish completed scans, or export SARIF, JSON, and CSV. [Integration workflows](docs/plugin-connectors.md). - Automate scans across repositories or project components, including in CI and containers. ## Use in Codex Open your repository in a Codex session with the Codex Security plugin enabled, then ask: > Run a Codex Security scan on this repository, focusing on authentication and > authorization. Return the saved report, source evidence, and coverage limits. A completed scan saves a report and findings. Read the report for source evidence and exclusions, then request a patch or ask Codex to verify an existing fix. See the [agent workflow guide](docs/agent-workflows.md) for setup, task selection, and recovery. ## Quick start Requires Node.js 22.13.0+ within 22.x, or Node.js 24.x or 26.x, and Python 3.10+. Python 3.10 also requires `tomli`. Install the CLI globally and sign in: ```bash npm install --global @openai/codex-security cs login ``` Run your first scan from the repository directory: ```bash cs scan . ``` When the scan completes, open the Markdown file at the **REPORT** path in the terminal. Run `cs scans show` from the same repository to find its latest completed scan again. See [scan scope and follow-up work](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#understand-scan-scope-and-follow-up-work) for how to interpret exclusions in the report. `cs` and `codex-security` run the same CLI. If the short name conflicts with another command, use `codex-security`. To skip the global install, or if npm reports an `EEXIST` conflict, use `npx @openai/codex-security` in place of `cs` for both login and scanning. For CI, set `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `CODEX_API_KEY` in the scan process's environment. For a headless machine, see [device or SSH login](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#authentication). ### Scan options Choose a scope and scan mode: ```bash # Scan selected paths. cs scan . --path src --path tests # Scan committed changes from a base revision to HEAD. cs scan . --diff origin/main # Run a deep scan of the repository. cs scan . --mode deep ``` Use `cs scan . --max-time 15` for an advisory 15-minute Standard investigation allowance. See [investigation time](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#set-investigation-time) for timing semantics and Deep Scan limits. Use `cs --help` to browse commands, or `cs scan --help` for scan options, cost limits, and patching after a scan. For an application spread across repositories, see [review one system across repositories](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#review-one-system-across-repositories). Use [bulk scans](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#bulk-scans) for independent repository reviews in one resumable campaign. Scans use existing root and component `SECURITY.md` guidance. Either way, the iPhone must be paired with the target Apple Watch, and the Watch must run a supported watchOS version. #### Install the IPA > **Known issue with Sideloadly 0.72:** [Issue #43](https://github.com/pookjw/HermesEnabler/issues/43) reports that this version may remove the embedded Watch app while signing. If the iPhone app installs but HermesEnabler2 is missing from the Watch, use Xcode instead. This report is specific to version 0.72; compatibility with other versions has not been confirmed. 1. Download the IPA from [Releases](https://github.com/pookjw/HermesEnabler/releases). 2. Install [Sideloadly](https://sideloadly.io) on your Mac, connect your iPhone with a cable, and select it in Sideloadly. 3. Drag the IPA into Sideloadly and enter your Apple ID. Turn off **Use automatic bundle ID**, set a fixed Bundle Identifier, and start signing. 4. On the iPhone, open **Settings → General → VPN & Device Management** and trust your developer certificate. 5. On the iPhone, open **Settings → Privacy & Security → Developer Mode**, turn it on, restart, and confirm. 6. On the iPhone, open the **Watch** app, go to **My Watch → Apps**, and install **HermesEnabler2** on the Watch. 7. On the Apple Watch, open **Settings → Privacy & Security → Developer Mode**, turn it on, restart, and confirm. If the option is not shown, install the Watch app first and check again. 8. Open **HermesEnabler2** on your Apple Watch and follow the steps in the app. #### Build with Xcode 1. Open [HermesEnabler2.xcodeproj](HermesEnabler2.xcodeproj) in Xcode. 2. Select your Apple Watch as the run destination and click **Run**. 3. Open **HermesEnabler2** on your Apple Watch and follow the steps in the app. ### Windows Windows uses [WatchBridge](https://github.com/AdminZachary/iloader-for-windows), a community tool that prepares Developer Mode and installs an IPA containing both an iPhone host app and a Watch app. It is not affiliated with Apple or with this project. 1. Install **Apple Mobile Device Service** by installing [iTunes](https://www.apple.com/itunes/) or the **Apple Devices** app from the Microsoft Store. WatchBridge needs it for USB and Wi-Fi communication. WebView2 is built into Windows 11. 2. Make sure your iPhone is paired with the target Apple Watch. WatchBridge supports only one paired Watch at a time; if more than one is paired, the preparation step stops instead of guessing. 3. Download `watchbridge-windows.zip` from [WatchBridge Releases](https://github.com/AdminZachary/iloader-for-windows/releases/latest), extract it, and run `WatchBridge.exe`. The executable is unsigned, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first launch. 4. Download the IPA from [Releases](https://github.com/pookjw/HermesEnabler/releases). Use the original IPA that contains both the iPhone host and the `Watch/*.app`; Watch-only packages are not supported. 5. Connect the paired iPhone over USB and select it in WatchBridge. 6. Pair the Watch and confirm the trust prompt on the Watch. Request the **Developer Mode** switch, then on the Watch open **Settings → Privacy & Security → Developer Mode**, turn it on, restart, and confirm. Return to WatchBridge and click **Check again**. WatchBridge does not enable Developer Mode or restart the Watch for you. 7. Sign in with your Apple ID, select the HermesEnabler2 IPA, and start signing and installation. WatchBridge installs the iPhone host app first, then the Watch app. 8. Open **HermesEnabler2** on your Apple Watch and follow the steps in the app. > Developer-mode preparation r

repositories.readme_excerpt: # TensorFold TensorFold serves language models from a Zig binary on Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs. The engine reads checkpoints, tokenizes requests and runs Metal or CUDA kernels directly. Serving needs no Python or MLX installation. Building with a coding agent? Have it load the [contributor skill](docs/recipes/SKILL.md) before it writes any code. ## Contributing with agents Please use [Agent Traffic Control](https://github.com/ashhart/ATC) before editing TensorFold so contributors and agents can avoid duplicate work and conflicting changes. Check the [live agent radar](https://tensorfold.dev/atc) before choosing an issue and follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [ATC contributor instructions](docs/atc/SKILL.md). Install or upgrade ATC to 0.9.4 or later, then run from an updated TensorFold clone: ```sh npm install -g github:ashhart/ATC atc check ISSUE --json atc claim ISSUE --json ``` Replace `ISSUE` with the issue number and claim only after a complete check says the work is free. TensorFold enables automatic public check-ins: a successful new claim starts an anonymous session on the radar and returns its `session` number. Keep that number instead of starting a duplicate session. For work already yours, start a session with `atc start ISSUE --json`. Add `--github-name` to `claim` or `start` only if you want your verified GitHub name shown; `--local` keeps a new session on your machine. The board shows the issue, activity state and last check-in; GitHub still associates the verification comment with its author. Check that `publication` is `public`; `unavailable` means the public update failed even if the local claim or session succeeded. Pulse only while the agent is working, before its five-minute check-in expires: ```sh atc pulse ISSUE SESSION working --json atc who path/to/file --json atc overlap --json atc land ISSUE SESSION --json atc release ISSUE --json ``` Use `reviewing` or `blocked` when appropriate, land the session when it stops, and resolve overlaps before opening a pull request. Before opening a pull request, have the agent run the [pull request skill](docs/pr/SKILL.md); agents that support skills can install it as `tensorfold-pull-request`. ## Quick start Start with Qwen3.5-2B, the small 4-bit checkpoint checked on Metal and a GB10. The commands below download its pinned revision, then serve it as `local-model`. Model weights have their own licenses. Reviewing or benchmarking TensorFold? [Evaluating TensorFold](docs/evaluating.md) covers pinning, signature checks, a container and the tests that need no GPU. ### Mac with Apple Silicon Install with Homebrew, then start the server: ```sh brew install ashhart/tensorfold/tensorfold tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3 tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking ``` ### Linux with an NVIDIA GPU Use the release archive for your CPU: `linux-aarch64` on a GB10, `linux-x86_64` on an x86_64 host. It needs glibc 2.28 or newer and NVIDIA driver R580 or newer (CUDA 13.0), providing `libcuda.so.1`. Keep the archive's directories together. Its kernels are built with CUDA 13, so TensorFold refuses an older driver at startup; `nvidia-smi` shows the installed one. See the [CUDA runbook](RUNBOOK.md#linux-and-cuda) for runtime libraries and supported GPUs. ```sh V=1.2.7 case "$(uname -m)" in aarch64|arm64) PLATFORM=linux-aarch64 ;; x86_64) PLATFORM=linux-x86_64 ;; *) echo 'No release archive for this CPU' >&2; exit 1 ;; esac curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" sha256sum -c "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" tar -xzf "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" export PATH="$PWD/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM/bin:$PATH" tensorfold() { command tensorfold-native "$@"; } tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.

# Node.js Node.js is an open-source, cross-platform JavaScript runtime environment. For information on using Node.js, see the [Node.js website][]. The Node.js project uses an [open governance model](./GOVERNANCE.md). The [OpenJS Foundation][] provides support for the project. Contributors are expected to act in a collaborative manner to move the project forward. We encourage the constructive exchange of contrary opinions and compromise. The [TSC](./GOVERNANCE.md#technical-steering-committee) reserves the right to limit or block contributors who repeatedly act in ways that discourage, exhaust, or otherwise negatively affect other participants. **This project has a [Code of Conduct][].** ## Table of contents * [Support](#support) * [Release types](#release-types) * [Download](#download) * [Current and LTS releases](#current-and-lts-releases) * [Nightly releases](#nightly-releases) * [API documentation](#api-documentation) * [Verifying binaries](#verifying-binaries) * [Building Node.js](#building-nodejs) * [Security](#security) * [Contributing to Node.js](#contributing-to-nodejs) * [Current project team members](#current-project-team-members) * [TSC (Technical Steering Committee)](#tsc-technical-steering-committee) * [Collaborators](#collaborators) * [Triagers](#triagers) * [Release keys](#release-keys) * [License](#license) ## Support Looking for help? Check out the [instructions for getting support](.github/SUPPORT.md). ## Release types Node.js follows [semantic versioning](https://semver.org). * **Alpha**: Under active development where semver-major changes are allowed. Each October, a new release line (for example, Node.js 27) branches off `main` and receives Alpha releases (for example, `27.0.0-alpha.0.0.0`) for 6 months, then are promoted to Current (see below) each April. Alpha releases are signed, tagged, and tested through [CITGM](https://github.com/nodejs/citgm), but their API and ABI may change between releases. They are intended for library authors and CI pipelines, not for production use. * **Current**: Under active development, no semver-major changes allowed. Node.js releases a new major version once a year, in April. Releases stay Current for 6 months, then convert to LTS (see below) each October. Their ABI may change between releases. They are intended for library authors and CI pipelines, not for production use. * **LTS**: Releases under Long Term Support, with a focus on stability and security. Only changes that have been on Alpha or Current release for two weeks can be backported to a typical LTS release. Every major version becomes an LTS release, and receives 30 months of LTS support, for a total of 36 months from its first Current release to End-of-Life. LTS release lines have alphabetically-ordered code names, beginning with Node.js 4 Argon. * **Nightly**: Code from the `main` branch built every 24-hours when there are changes. Unlike Alpha releases, nightly builds are automated and untested. Use with caution. # Agent Skills **Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.** Skills encode the workflows, quality gates, and best practices that senior engineers use when building software. These ones are packaged so AI agents follow them consistently across every phase of development. ![Addy's Agent Skills](https://addyosmani.com/assets/images/addys-agent-skills.jpg) ``` DEFINE PLAN BUILD VERIFY REVIEW SHIP ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ │ Idea │ ───▶ │ Spec │ ───▶ │ Code │ ───▶ │ Test │ ───▶ │ QA │ ───▶ │ Go │ │Refine│ │ PRD │ │ Impl │ │Debug │ │ Gate │ │ Live │ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ /spec /plan /build /test /review /ship ``` --- ## Commands 9 slash commands that map to the development lifecycle. Each one activates the right skills automatically. | What you're doing | Command | Key principle | |-------------------|---------|---------------| | Define what to build | `/spec` | Spec before code | | Plan how to build it | `/plan` | Small, atomic tasks | | Build incrementally | `/build` | One slice at a time | | Prove it works | `/test` | Tests are proof | | Set the quality bar | `/constraints` | Decide it once, enforce it everywhere | | Review before merge | `/review` | Improve code health | | Audit web performance | `/webperf` | Measure before you optimize | | Simplify the code | `/code-simplify` | Clarity over cleverness | | Ship to production | `/ship` | Faster is safer | In Claude Code these install as plugin commands. Where a built-in command has the same name, as `/review` does, use the namespaced form: `/agent-skills:review`. Want fewer manual steps once the spec exists? **`/build auto`** generates the plan and implements every task in a single approved pass — you approve the plan once, then it runs autonomously. It removes the human stepping *between* tasks, not the verification: every task is still test-driven and committed individually, and it pauses on failures or risky steps. Skills also activate automatically based on what you're doing — designing an API triggers `api-and-interface-design`, building UI triggers `frontend-ui-engineering`, and so on. --- ## Quick Start **Fastest path — any agent, one command.** The open [skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) installs into 70+ agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Cline, and more): ```bash npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills # install all 25 skills npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --list # browse before installing ``` Or grab individual skills: ```bash npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --skill code-review-and-quality # five-axis review before merge npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --skill interview-me # requirements interrogation, one question at a time npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --skill test-driven-development # red-green-refactor, enforced ``` > **Installing one skill?** A per-skill `npx` install copies only > `skills//`, not the repo-level `references/` directory.
